run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T00:59:28Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy corresponds to a real, observed jump in that proxy's own error spans: its ingress error rate went from ~0/s (occasional ≤0.017/s) to ~0.96/s at 01:00:28 and ~1.9–2.1/s from 01:02:28 to 01:10:28, with ingress spans carrying http.status_code 504 at ~15.0 s duration and its logs showing "504 UT response_timeout" for GET /api/products/{id} (14999 ms) and GET /api/recommendations (15000 ms). The failing path is frontend -> product-catalog: the frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct had p90 54–64 ms from 00:36:28 to 00:58:28 and then 15000 ms at 01:02:28, while product-catalog's own server span p90 stayed ~1.8 ms throughout, i.e. the delay was on the network path, not in product-catalog's application. Kubernetes events (all namespaces) show chaos-mesh NetworkChaos objects named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-* being Started/Applied every minute from 00:57:27, each with the message "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9", and a chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay emitting "Create new object: otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-*" at the same times. Hypothesis (strongly supported, not proven from the CR spec): this scheduled network-delay injection on the product-catalog pod caused the ~15 s frontend→product-catalog calls, the frontend-proxy 15 s upstream timeouts (504) and the checkout/frontend 500s (product lookup failed with gRPC status 14 connection reset). The Schedule's spec could not be read, its creation time is unknown, and whether the fault was still being applied after 01:05:27 is unknown, so the conclusion is partial. Checked and not implicated: product-catalog application latency, frontend-proxy/frontend/product-catalog pod state (all Running, 0 restarts), and a separate fraud-detection container restart at 00:53:43 (last state OOMKilled) whose own error rate stayed at 0 or ≤0.0037/s.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, service_name=frontend-proxy, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) were 0 with occasional values ≤0.017/s up to 00:58:28, then jumped to 0.963/s at 01:00:28, 1.94/s at 01:02:28, 1.93/s at 01:04:28, 2.02/s at 01:06:28, 1.99/s at 01:08:28 and 1.21/s at 01:10:28; the rise is on span_name "ingress", and the "router frontend egress" client span errors begin at 01:04:28.

Across all services, the error-span rate at 01:00:28–01:10:28 is elevated only for frontend-proxy (up to 2.07/s) and frontend (0.40/s at 01:04:28, 0.63/s at 01:08:28, 0.74/s at 01:10:28); accounting, cart and payment stay at 0, ad and recommendation show only sporadic values ≤0.0039/s, and fraud-detection shows 0 except ≤0.0037/s around 00:56–00:58.

In the error=true sample for frontend-proxy, 9 of 14 "ingress" spans carry http.status_code 504 with duration ≈15.0 s and 1 carries 500; the same traces contain the frontend POST /api/checkout span (status 500) with exception.message "13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #\"0PUK6V6EV0\"", the checkout span oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (rpc.grpc.status_code 13, "failed to prepare order: failed to get product #\"0PUK6V6EV0\"") and the checkout client span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (rpc.grpc.status_code 14, otel.status_description "error reading from server: read tcp 100.96.4.114:59432->100.64.188.136:8080: read: connection reset by peer").

frontend-proxy pod logs (pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d) record "GET /api/products/6E92ZMYYFZ HTTP/1.1\" 504 UT response_timeout" with 14999 ms and "GET /api/recommendations?productIds=OLJCESPC7Z HTTP/1.1\" 504 UT response_timeout" with 15000 ms at 01:05:33–01:05:34, so the 504s are upstream timeouts rather than proxy-local failures.

The frontend's client span grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct had histogram_quantile(0.9) of 54–64 ms at every point from 00:36:28 through 00:58:28 (baseline), then 109 ms at 01:00:28 and 15000 ms at 01:02:28 — a jump to the same ~15 s timeout seen at the proxy.

product-catalog's own server span oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct kept histogram_quantile(0.9) at ~1.80–1.88 ms across 00:36:28–01:06:28, i.e. product-catalog application processing did not slow down while its callers saw 15 s calls.

chaos-mesh events show NetworkChaos objects named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-jj42n, -6rtdg, -bx27q, -x5l64, -b5dxg, -gjgf2, -d9vpw, -26dqc and -hcwrz each emitting "Experiment has started" and "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9" at 00:57:27, 00:58:27, 00:59:27, 01:00:27, 01:01:27, 01:02:27, 01:03:27, 01:04:27 and 01:05:27 respectively, with "Time up according to the duration" and "Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9" about 55 s later; PodNetworkChaos updates for the same pod name are recorded at those times.

A Schedule named otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay in namespace chaos-mesh emitted Spawned events "Create new object: otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-<suffix>" once per minute at 00:57:27, 00:58:27, 00:59:27, 01:00:27, 01:01:27, 01:02:27, 01:03:27, 01:04:27 and 01:05:27, matching the NetworkChaos objects named in the "Successfully apply chaos" messages.

Grouping all events in the authorized window by involved-object kind, namespace and reason gives NetworkChaos in chaos-mesh (Started 9, Applied 9, TimeUp 8, Recovered 8, Updated 68, FinalizerInited 17), Schedule in chaos-mesh (Spawned 9, Updated 9) and PodNetworkChaos in otel-demo (Updated 17); no other fault-injection kind appears.

Pod state at query time: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 Running/ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 00:21:35, frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-xh66d Running/ready with 0 restarts, and frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr Running/ready with 0 restarts — so none of the three was restarted during the incident.

Traffic through the delayed dependency collapsed: the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct call rate fell from ~8.0–9.9/s before 00:58:28 to 3.99/s at 01:00:28, 0.21/s at 01:02:28 and 0 at 01:04:28, its GET /api/products/{productId} span rate fell from ~4.1–5.0/s to 0 at 01:04:28, and product-catalog's oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct server rate fell from ~8.9–11.0/s to 0.33/s at 01:04:28, 0.07/s at 01:06:28 and 0 at 01:08:28.

Trace 5050bceaec29062560a2f07f3a99cc90 shows the frontend-proxy ingress span erroring with http.status_code 504 after 15000376 us, its "router frontend egress" child span (error=true, http.status_code 0) after 15000225 us, while the frontend GET span for the same request ran 15881753 us and recorded http.status_code 200 — the proxy gave up on an upstream request that the frontend was still serving.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-n7vmf restarted during the window: container events Created/Started at 00:53:43, pod restartCount 2 with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, and its error-span rate stayed at 0 except ≤0.0037/s around 00:56–00:58 — a separate event that precedes and does not scale with the frontend-proxy error burst.

The chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay repeatedly injected a network delay into pod otel-demo/product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9 every minute from 00:57:27; frontend→product-catalog calls then took ~15 s (client p90 60 ms → 15000 ms) while product-catalog's own processing stayed ~1.8 ms, so the frontend's product/recommendation routes exceeded frontend-proxy's ~15 s upstream timeout and produced the 504 ingress errors that raised the RequestErrorRate alert.

frontend-proxy itself being broken (config/resource/restart) is not supported: the pod has 0 restarts and is ready, and its log lines for the failed requests are "504 UT response_timeout", i.e. an upstream response timeout rather than a local proxy fault.

product-catalog application slowness or crash is not supported: its server-side GetProduct p90 stayed ~1.8 ms, its pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts, and no NetworkChaos/other event names any other otel-demo pod.

The fraud-detection OOMKill/restart at 00:53:43 is not a plausible cause of this alert: it happened before the error-rate jump, its own error-span rate remained 0 or ≤0.0037/s, and the observed failing dependency in the checkout error was product-catalog ("failed to get product", gRPC status 14 connection reset).

Treat the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay (namespace chaos-mesh) as test fault injection and have its owner confirm/stop it; if the demo is not supposed to run this experiment, remove the Schedule so the NetworkChaos objects stop being spawned every minute against product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-7rqh9.

gaps: The chaos-mesh Schedule and NetworkChaos specs could not be read with the permitted Kubernetes kinds (only listed built-in kinds are readable), so the injected delay value, duration, direction and target selector are unknown, and when the Schedule was created or last changed is unknown (change_history integration is not available).

NetworkChaos events end at 01:05:27 (last object otel-demo-product-catalog-network-delay-hcwrz, no TimeUp/Recovered returned for it), yet frontend-proxy's error rate was still 1.21/s at 01:10:28 and error spans exist with start time 01:06:24; whether the network delay was still being applied after 01:05:27 is unknown.
fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-64blr returned 0 bytes/lines for 00:50:00–01:14:44Z, so frontend's own application error text for this incident is unchecked.

The filtered product-catalog log query (err|error|fail|timeout|reset) matched none of the 5000 lines read (read through 01:04:41Z); no product-catalog error text was observed, but that is not proof of absence and later lines were not read.
list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the alert's expression, threshold and the exact 1.42 value in the annotation are unverified.

traces_search_by_tags for recommendation error=true in 00:55–01:14 returned no matching trace, although recommendation's error-span metric showed sporadic ~0.0037/s; whether those sporadic recommendation errors relate to the product-catalog delay was not established.

Only traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket had series in the window; rpc_*, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count and kube_deployment_* series were not returned, so latency had to be judged from trace span histograms and pod-level state from kube-state-metrics was not available for this window.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
